az_farmhouse_the.blurb: The Farmhouse is a cliff band in the Sonoita area of southern Arizona, at about 5,400 ft, reached from Highway 82 east of Whetstone. The cliff faces north, so much of it stays shaded, which gives it a long climbing season. The climbing is almost all sport on steep to vertical walls, with a walk in of roughly 30 to 45 minutes. Grades run from 5.7 to 5.14, with most routes between 5.10 and 5.12 and a few moderates. The Bowling Alley, a steep overhang with consistent shade, holds the most climbs. Vineyard and Whippersnapper Wall come next, with The Gap and The Prow nearby, and development is still ongoing.

ca_hartley_springs.blurb: Hartley Springs is a bouldering area near June Lake in the Eastern Sierra, at about 8,200 ft, with several separate sections spread through Jeffrey pine forest. The rock is volcanic tuff with pockets, slots and the occasional crack, and most boulders have flat pumice landings. Boulders are less than ten minutes' walk from the parking area. Grades run from VB to V9. The altitude makes it a spring through late fall destination. Mad Max Area holds the most climbs, followed by Warm Up Ridge, Road Boulder Area and Warm Up Area.

ca_hvcg_bouldering_circuit.blurb: The HVCG Bouldering Circuit is a large set of boulder problems in Joshua Tree National Park, in and around Hidden Valley Campground at about 4,200 ft. Because it is so big, it is divided by compass direction into HVCG West, North, South and East. HVCG West holds the most climbs, with HVCG North next. All of it is bouldering, from VB to V7, with most problems at V3 and under. Many problems need little or no approach, and some have crack features.

ca_phantom_spires.blurb: Phantom Spires is a group of granite spires high on a ridge north of Highway 50 in the Lake Tahoe area, at about 6,000 ft. The rock is black-and-white granite, less smooth than typical Tahoe granite; on Middle Spire it is frictiony and often knobby. Most of the climbing is trad, with some sport and a bouldering section of eleven problems. Roped routes run from 5.6 to 5.12, centred on 5.10 and 5.11. The setting is open and exposed and can be very windy, and the area is best from late fall through early summer. Upper Spire holds the most climbs, followed by Middle Spire, Lower Spire and Phantom Wall.

il_house_boulders.blurb: House Boulders is a bouldering area in southern Illinois, on the western edge of the Shawnee National Forest in the Mississippi Bluffs region, with views over the Mississippi River valley. It is a tightly stacked boulder field of about 20 acres on a steep, west-facing hillside among hardwood trees, next to the Holy Boulders. The rock is fine-grained sandstone. Problems run from V0 to V10, with most between V1 and V3 and a solid tail of V5 and harder. Hillside Boulders holds the most climbs, followed by State Property and Dawg Pound Boulder.

me_shagg_crag.blurb: Shagg Crag is a granite cliff in the Western Mountains of Maine, near Woodstock and about an hour from North Conway, New Hampshire. The granite is steep and juggy. Most routes are sport, with a few trad lines and a small bouldering section. Roped grades run from 5.7 upward, with the largest share at 5.12 and 5.13 and some moderate 5.10s and 5.11s; the boulder problems go from V0 to V8. The crag gets afternoon sun with little shade, which suits sunny winter days but runs hot in summer. The walk in takes roughly 30 minutes. Main Face holds the most climbs, with Right End and Main Face Linkups next.
